For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

Symptom relief was reported in 26 of 30 patients with available symptom data (86.7%). Anticancer treatment continued without interruption in 24 of 33 patients (72.7%). These denominators differ because not all patients had symptom data recorded.

**What the Results Support**

The series supports feasibility: high-dose oral vitamin D was administered alongside ongoing anticancer therapy without reported treatment-related adverse events, and most patients maintained their cancer treatment schedule. The observed symptom relief in the majority of those assessed is encouraging as a signal warranting further study.

**Limits of Causal and Safety Claims**

Causation cannot be inferred. Thirty of 33 patients received concurrent supportive therapy, and no untreated or placebo-controlled comparator existed, so improvement cannot be attributed to vitamin D alone. The 10-day observation window and inconsistent post-treatment laboratory data (vitamin D levels measured in only 13 patients) preclude conclusions about general safety.
